# Incident Report: Malware Infection — DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (2024-08-15)

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `plucero`, both from the host itself and from the domain controller at 10.8.15.4) |

## Malware Family

**Latrodectus** loader — **behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alert files were provided with this evidence set, and no static signature/YARA match was performed. Attribution rests on the following observed traffic characteristics, which match publicly documented Latrodectus TTPs:

- Fake-invoice ZIP phishing lure delivering a heavily padded/obfuscated `.js` downloader.
- Use of native Windows BITS (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` User-Agent, i.e. `bitsadmin`/`Start-BitsTransfer`) to fetch a second-stage PE32+ DLL directly from a raw IP address over plain HTTP.
- Persistent HTTP GET `/` and POST `/` beaconing to that same raw IP on port 80, using the User-Agent `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the malformed extra space after "Mozilla"), with a large base64-like blob carried in the `Cookie` header and binary/encrypted POST bodies — the exact C2 signature pattern reported for Latrodectus.

## Infection Chain (as observed in the capture)

1. **T+74.7s** — Host resolves `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159, Cloudflare-fronted) and downloads a ZIP via a fake-FedEx phishing page: `GET /managements?...` → response `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoice 876597035_003.zip"`. SHA256 of the ZIP: `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5`.
   - Inside the ZIP: `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (SHA256 `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`), a ~6.9 MB JScript file padded with megabytes of decoy text/library code to evade static AV detection.
2. **T+135.9s** — `bitsadmin`/BITS (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) issues `HEAD` then `GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` to **72.5.43.29:80**, downloading a PE32+ x86-64 DLL. SHA256: `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` (159,232 bytes).
3. **T+196.9s through end of capture (T+1962s / ~30 min)** — Sustained C2 beaconing: 308 HTTP requests (GET `/` and POST `/`, roughly every 5–10 seconds initially, slowing to 5–10 minute intervals) to **72.5.43.29:80**, no DNS lookup performed (hardcoded IP), UA `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` (HTTP) — malware C2/second-stage host, contacted directly by IP with no DNS resolution.

**Malicious/phishing domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159 (referenced link, `/data-privacy`)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — ZIP delivery
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — second-stage DLL download via BITS
- `http://72.5.43.29/` — ongoing C2 GET/POST beacon URL

**Transferred files and hashes**
| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Invoice 876597035_003.zip | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Phishing lure ZIP |
| Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | JS downloader inside ZIP |
| 0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 (BITS payload) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | PE32+ x64 DLL, second-stage payload, delivered via BITS from the C2 IP |

## Notes on non-malicious traffic

`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `oneocsp.microsoft.com`, and `acroipm2.adobe.com/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` are legitimate Windows Update/OCSP/Adobe telemetry traffic and were ruled out as related to the infection.
